question: m01
q: Are real wages going up? Compare wage growth from the ABS Wage Price Index with inflation.

transcript.answer:
**No. Real wages are falling.** Wage growth has been below inflation for the past several quarters, and the gap widened in 2026.

| Period | WPI wage growth (y/y, Australia, private and public, total hourly rates excl. bonuses) | CPI inflation (y/y, all groups) | Real wage growth (approx.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 Q3 | 3.3% | 3.6% (Sep 2025) | -0.3 pts |
| 2025 Q4 | 3.4% | 3.8% (Dec 2025) | -0.4 pts |
| 2026 Q1 | 3.2% | 4.6% (Mar 2026) | -1.4 pts |
| 2026 Q2 | 3.2% | 3.8% (Jun 2026) | -0.6 pts |
| Latest | 3.2% (Q2 2026) | 4.0% (Aug 2026) | about -0.8 pts |

Using the RBA's preferred measure, the trimmed mean, inflation was 3.6% in August 2026, so real wages were still about 0.4 points behind.

Some context:
- **Wages are growing, just more slowly than prices.** Wage growth has been steady at about 3.2–3.4% since mid-2025.
- **Inflation has picked up.** Headline CPI rose from 1.9% in June 2025 to a peak of 4.6% in March 2026 and was 4.0% in August 2026.
- **Real wages were positive in 2024 and early 2025.** In those periods wage growth was 3.5–4%, above inflation, so this is a recent reversal.

Caveats:
- I used total hourly rates excluding bonuses for the WPI, because the ordinary-time series key did not return data. The two are close in concept.
- The comparison uses the quarterly WPI against monthly CPI, so the gaps are approximate.
- The latest WPI is the June 2026 quarter. The September 2026 quarter is due in November.
